findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, making the MySQL database reachable from the internet. This expands the attack surface beyond the private network.
storage_encrypted = false disables encryption of the database volume, leaving sensitive customer data at rest unencrypted.

skip_final_snapshot = true combined with backup_retention_period = 0 means no backups are retained, so the only available snapshot is skipped on destroy; this is a data-loss/availability gap but also leaves no recoverable copy of sensitive data, and apply_immediately = true can cause availability disruption during maintenance.

The EC2 user_data script embeds the RDS database password via ${var.password} in plaintext in the instance user data. This exposes the database credentials to anyone able to read the instance metadata/launch configuration and leaves them stored in plaintext on the instance.

The IAM policy grants wildcard actions (s3:*, ec2:*, rds:*) on all resources to any EC2 instance assuming this role. This is an overly permissive, least-privilege-violating policy that allows broad data access and infrastructure modification.

The ingress rule allows TCP 3306 (MySQL) from the entire VPC CIDR. While scoped to the VPC, combined with publicly_accessible = true and the egress rule permitting all traffic, this exposes the database to any host in the VPC and contributes to weak network segmentation.

The egress rule permits all outbound traffic (protocol -1, ports 0-0) to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing the database to communicate with arbitrary external hosts, which is unnecessary and expands blast radius in the event of compromise.

The DB subnet group references web_subnet and web_subnet2 (web-tier public subnets) rather than dedicated private subnets, so the RDS instance is placed on the VPC's public network segment rather than an isolated database tier.

findings.issue_category: unrestricted ingress / no encryption in transit
findings.description: The instance does not set a CA certificate or require SSL/TLS (no ssl enforced), and the MySQL connection is made in plaintext in the user-data PHP script, transmitting database credentials and data in cleartext across the network.
